learning_objective: 🎯 [Kids will understand the concept of gender in nouns and learn to classify them into Masculine, Feminine, Common, and Neuter genders.]
warm_up_hook: 👑 Kings and Queens, Boys and Girls! Did you know that nouns belong to different families called 'Genders'? Let's meet the boys, the girls, and everything else in the Noun Family!

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Nouns that refer to males (boys, men, or male animals) are of the Masculine Gender. Nouns that refer to females (girls, women, or female animals) are of the Feminine Gender.
Some names can be used for BOTH males and females. We call these Common Gender nouns. When you hear these words, it could be a boy or a girl!
examples_or_templates: Baby (can be a baby boy or a baby girl)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Things that do not have life (non-living things) are neither male nor female. They belong to the Neuter Gender. 'Neuter' means neither!

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ What is the Feminine gender of 'Tiger'?
❓ Which of these is a Neuter Gender noun?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Change the gender in this sentence: 'The king was very happy with his son.'
subjective_practice.hint: Change 'king' to the female word, and 'son' to the female word.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Sort these words into Common and Neuter: Friend, Pencil, Cousin, Shoe.
subjective_practice.hint: Which ones are alive and can be a boy/girl? Which ones are objects?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write the Masculine word for 'Cow' and 'Hen'.
subjective_practice.hint: Think of the male animals on a farm. One has horns, the other crows in the morning!

activity_or_assignment.title: ✂️ The Gender Sorting Game
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Draw four columns on a paper: Masculine, Feminine, Common, Neuter. Pick up any storybook, find 10 naming words (nouns), and put them in the correct column!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Masculine nouns are for males (boy, uncle).
⭐ Feminine nouns are for females (girl, aunt).
⭐ Common nouns are for both males and females (friend, baby).
⭐ Neuter nouns are for non-living things (desk, cup).
